Bar New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Вінницька область, Ukraine

Not demolished. Bar's Jewish community, first mentioned in 1542, is among the oldest in Ukraine; an agreement in 1556 granted Bar's Jews the right to own buildings and share the same rights and duties as other residents, though they were forbidden from lodging Jewish visitors in the city. The community suffered massacres during the Khmelnytsky uprising in 1648 and again by Cossacks and Tatars in 1651, but grew to 5,773 (58 percent) by 1897 and 10,450 (46 percent) by 1910, with Jews owning most of the town's shops, its only pharmacy, and factories across numerous industries. Twenty Jews died in a 1919 pogrom. The Germans occupied Bar on July 16, 1941, establishing two ghettos that December, where most of the town's remaining Jews were murdered or died. This new cemetery, established during the Soviet period on the city's northern outskirts, holds about 1,500 matzevot.
